examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Between Zero and One
examples.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x}+2 & \ge 12 \\ 5\cdot {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x} & \ge 10 \\ {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{3}{4})}^{x}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{4}) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\ln 3 - \ln 4$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\cdot {3}^{2x-1} & \ge 2 \\ {3}^{2x-1} & \ge 8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the logarithm to base $3$ of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{3}⁡({3}^{2x-1}) & \ge {log}_{3}⁡(8) \\ 2x-1 & \ge {log}_{3}⁡(8) \\ 2x & \ge {log}_{3}⁡(8)+1 \\ x & \ge \frac{1}{2}({log}_{3}⁡(8)+1).\end{aligned}
$$
